title: Security team: who leads security, whom do they report to, and who do you hire next?
short: Within 30 days, name a head of security with a deputy and a direct line to management, outside IT operations.
answer: Within 30 days, have management appoint one head of security or ISB in writing, with a named deputy and a direct reporting line to the managing directors, outside IT operations. Then add people in the order your biggest risks need them, describe each role with an ECSF profile, and buy any work you can't keep a person busy with.
audience: Managing directors, heads of security and IT leads who also own security, in small and mid-size companies and regulated organizations

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Appoint one owner in writing.
items.text: Have management name a head of security or ISB, a deputy and their authority in a minuted decision. ENISA lists formal appointments, job descriptions and evidence of competence as NIS2 proof[^enisatig].

items.title: Give them a direct line to management.
items.text: Digital providers need at least one person reporting directly to the management body[^nis2ir]. The BSI asks German NIS2 managers to confirm the ISB or CISO reporting line early[^bsicurr].

items.title: Keep oversight out of IT operations.
items.text: The BSI advises against placing the ISB in the IT department, because of role conflicts[^std2002]. Security engineering can sit in IT; the person who checks it shouldn't.

items.title: Give every security role a deputy.
items.text: ENISA advises a deputy for each security role[^enisatig]; the BSI says the ISB needs a qualified one[^std2002]. Let the deputy run the monthly report while the lead is away.

items.title: Hire for your top risk, buy the rest.
items.text: Buy work that specialists do a few days a year: penetration tests, forensics, 24/7 monitoring. In ENISA's 2025 survey, 45% named a lack of skilled candidates as the main hiring barrier[^nisinv].

blocks.title: Hire in this order
blocks.intro: Each step names the ECSF profile[^ecsfrp] and the closest NICE work role[^nice]. One person can cover several steps at first.

items.title: Head of security or ISB.
items.text: ECSF Chief Information Security Officer, which includes the ISB title; NICE Executive Cybersecurity Leadership. Owns strategy, policy, the ISMS and risk reporting.

items.title: Security engineer.
items.text: ECSF Cybersecurity Implementer; NICE Systems Security Analysis. Owns identity, endpoint and cloud controls with IT, among the skills most in demand[^nisinv].

items.title: Detection and response lead.
items.text: ECSF Cyber Incident Responder; NICE Incident Response. Runs the MDR contract and the incident plan. Detection and response topped ENISA's skills list, at 38%[^nisinv].

items.title: Risk and compliance.
items.text: ECSF Cybersecurity Risk Manager; NICE Cybersecurity Policy and Planning. Runs the risk register, regulatory evidence and customer questionnaires.

items.title: Architect or deputy head.
items.text: ECSF Cybersecurity Architect; NICE Cybersecurity Architecture. Reviews project designs and deputizes for the head.

blocks.title: Where the head of security reports
items: **Report to the CEO or managing director.** In ENISA's 2021 survey, its latest to ask, 56% of heads of information security reported to the CEO or board, 29% to the CIO or an IT executive and 14% to risk management[^nisinv21].
**A CRO or COO works if they don't run IT.** A reviewer must sit outside the line of authority of what they review, ENISA says[^enisatig]. Keep a direct right to report to the managing directors.

**Under a CIO, write safeguards down.** The BSI calls an active admin as ISB a likely conflict of interest[^std2002]. Grant what the BSIG grants federal ISBs: a direct right to report and protection from being penalized for the job[^bsig].

**Separate admin work from oversight.** Digital providers must segregate conflicting duties; micro entities may use management oversight or more logging instead[^nis2ir]. Under DORA, ICT risk oversight goes to an independent control function[^dora]. The operating model sheet covers the three lines.

blocks.title: How big the team should be
items: **About one in ten IT staff work on security.** The share was 10.6% in ENISA's 2025 survey, the lowest yet[^nisinv], with a German median of 9.4%[^nisinvdata]. Most respondents were large organizations[^nisinv], so treat it as a cross-check, not a target.

**Operations takes the largest share.** In ENISA's 2023 survey, operations held 40% of security staff, architecture and engineering 23%, governance and risk 21% and audit and compliance 16%[^nisinv23].

**Outsource operations, not governance.** 57% of those organizations used the most contractors in operations, only 9% in governance and risk; contractors were a median 20% of security staff[^nisinv23].

**Count the work, not the ratio.** List recurring tasks with hours per month: risk register, audits, questionnaires, project reviews, alerts, suppliers. Make sure two trained people can do each one, in-house or at a provider.

blocks.title: The ISB and the data protection officer in Germany
items: **The BSIG requires an ISB only of federal bodies.** They need a deputy, report independently and may not be penalized for the job[^bsig]. Copy that into your ISB's appointment.
**The ISB protects all information.** In the BSI's model, the ISB steers the security process, advises management and joins major projects, for paper as well as IT[^std2002].

**The DPO monitors data protection law.** Without instructions, reporting to the top level, possibly as an external[^gdpr]. Germany requires one from 20 people regularly processing personal data by computer, or for processing that needs a DPIA[^bdsg38].

**Keep the two apart.** A DPO who decides the purposes and means of processing has a conflict of interest, the CJEU ruled[^c453]. Grundschutz++ names DPO versus ISB as a conflict to avoid[^std3001]. Use two people; in small companies, an external DPO.

blocks.title: A virtual or fractional CISO
items: **It fits part-time work.** Below about 250 staff, for a first ISMS or between hires. The BSI sees an external ISB as useful in small companies[^std2002]; digital providers may give security roles to external parties[^nis2ir].

**Keep accountability and control in-house.** Responsibility and oversight can't be delegated, the BSI says[^bsicurr]. Keep an internal coordinator, risk acceptance, the decision to report an incident, admin and emergency credentials, and the asset and supplier lists.
**Write the contract for the bad day.** Name the person and a deputy, hours per month, incident response time, deliverables, document ownership and exit handover. See the third-party risk sheet.
**Don't hire your IT provider for it.** It would check its own work[^enisatig].

blocks.title: Hiring and keeping security staff
items: **Expect a skills gap.** In ENISA's 2025 survey, 94% of SMEs had trouble attracting security staff[^nisinv]. In ISC2's, 59% had critical or significant skills needs, up from 44%[^isc2].

**Test problem solving, not tool names.** Hiring managers in ISC2's survey ranked problem solving, teamwork and communication above any technical skill[^isc2]. Use a work sample from your own environment.

**Treat certificates as one filter.** Digital providers must check qualifications, for example by references, vetting, validated certifications or written tests[^nis2ir]. Pick training from ENISA's list of certifications mapped to ECSF profiles[^ecsfcert].

**Fund training, time and career steps.** 47% had no security training budget in ENISA's 2023 survey[^nisinv23]. Workload, weak training and few career steps topped the 2025 retention problems[^nisinv]. Give each person a budget and five protected days a year, and grow admins into engineers.

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **German management duties apply.** Under BSIG § 38, management implements and oversees the measures[^bsig]. The BSI's October 2026 curriculum asks it to confirm the ISB or CISO reporting line, ideally within 2 to 6 weeks of its first training[^bsicurr].
**Grundschutz++ names the conflicts.** BSI-Standard 300-1 of 20 October 2026 asks for roles with defined qualifications and no IT lead versus ISB or DPO versus ISB conflicts[^std3001].

**Germany plans to drop the 20-person DPO rule.** Federal and state leaders agreed on 4 December 2025 that the federal government will propose repealing it by the end of 2026, leaving GDPR Article 37[^fma]. It still applies[^bdsg38].

**The role catalogs are moving.** NICE v2.2.0 added a supply chain risk role in April 2026[^nice]. ENISA plans to consult on a revised ECSF with proficiency levels at the end of 2026[^ecsf]. Map to the current 12 profiles now.

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **A full-time CISO before there's a full-time job.** Below about 100 staff, a part-time ISB with a deputy, an IT provider and MDR cover it.
**An in-house 24/7 SOC.** A few analysts can't staff round-the-clock shifts. Buy MDR; see the SOC and MDR sheet.
**One hire per ECSF profile.** The 12 profiles describe work, not headcount.
**Certificates as the first filter.** Much of today's workforce came from other jobs through upskilling, ENISA notes[^nisinv]. Screen with a work sample.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Making the only admin the ISB.** They would judge their own work. If nobody else fits, buy an external ISB.
**One person who knows everything.** When they leave, the MDR contacts, admin paths and open risks leave too. Keep runbooks shared and have the deputy use them twice a year.
**A title without time or budget.** The BSI says security roles need qualified people with enough resources[^std2002]. Put hours per week and a budget into the appointment.
**Hiring a CISO without a mandate.** Agree budget, decision rights and reporting line before the first interview.

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Name an ISB with at least one day a week for the role, and a deputy. Not the only admin.
If nobody fits, buy an external ISB and keep a managing director as the internal owner.
Use an external DPO where you need one.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Make the first full-time hire a head of security who reports to a managing director.
Add a security engineer, then a detection and response lead who runs the MDR contract.
Write job descriptions against ECSF profiles.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Have the CISO report to the CEO or a board member who doesn't run IT, with a deputy who can sign.
Separate risk, policy and assurance from engineering; under DORA, as a control function[^dora].
Cross-check size: the German median in ENISA's 2025 survey was 19 security FTEs, including contractors[^nisinvdata].

changes.text: First draft, based on ENISA's NIS Investments reports and NIS2 guidance, the ECSF, NICE v2.2.0, ISC2's 2025 workforce study, Regulation 2024/2690, BSI-Standards 200-2 and 300-1, the BSIG, the GDPR, the BDSG and DORA.
